summary.headline: Premier Explosives Q1 FY27 revenue fell 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore, EBIT margin 4.7%, order book INR1,393 crore (94% defence).
summary.overview:
Revenue from operations declined 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore as dispatches and project execution slipped, mainly on export deliveries held up by maritime disruption and imported countermeasure components. EBIT fell 80% YoY to INR4.8 crore (4.7% margin) and PAT fell 80% to INR3 crore (3% margin), with raw material costs squeezing margins. Management said the export licence backlog is largely cleared and expects the delayed execution to complete in Q2 and Q3. Order book stands at INR1,393 crore, and FY27 revenue target is retained at about INR600 crore. Apollo Micro Systems' acquisition of promoter stake was discussed, with synergy details deferred to next quarter.</overview>

segments.name: Defence and Space
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 35% YoY per analyst question; management attributed delays to export licences and component imports, not customer acceptance. Defence is 94% of the order book.

segments.name: Industrial explosives / bulk
segments.commentary: About 6% of order book. Singareni execution of about INR25-30 crore remains for FY27; margins described as very thin, with some contracts negative. Coal India work withdrawn.

segments.name: Services (O&M)
segments.commentary: INR42 crore of order book (3%), no separate commentary on quarterly performance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target retained at about INR600 crore (analyst-reported INR600-700 crore earlier); management said Q1 revenue of about INR103 crore leaves 9 months to deliver INR500-600 crore.
EBITDA margin target of 15-20% for the year, reiterated; management said the gap in Q1 would be made up in coming quarters.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR200-300 crore; management said run rate of INR1,000 crore-plus per year over the next two years.
Export execution targeted at INR150-200 crore in Q2 FY27, with prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear in the quarter.
Order of INR430 crore (Oct 2025) to be fully executed in FY27 per management, versus earlier guidance of about two-thirds; Q1 execution was about INR21 crore.
Other expenses run-rate of INR9-10 crore per quarter cited as sustainable.
Katepally RDX/HMX water trials expected in September 2026 (about one month); mixing plant dummy trials expected by end September after imported mixer components are airlifted.
capex_capacity: Katepally: RDX and HMX plant integration and erection almost complete; water trials expected September 2026, lasting about one month before production.
Katepally mixing plant: 2.5 tonne planetary mixer installed; imported components delayed by shipping, now being airlifted; dummy trials targeted end-September 2026.
Andhra Pradesh expansion: land pricing unresolved; company has asked the state government to revise price. Management said Apollo would continue the expansion, with a decision after presentation.
Flares produced in own plant; production has started on the July 2023 flares order, with backlog of about INR75 crore to complete in 4-5 months. Chaff payload depends on imports, now executed.
Drones: company builds payloads and partners with drone makers as a partner, not a standalone supplier.
demand_pricing: Export licences: several received in the past week, with some in pipeline; material moving out of factories. Export of INR150-200 crore targeted in Q2.

INR350 crore international defence order (April 2026): export licence still in process; management said licence processing takes at least 3-4 months after importing-country import licence; some dispatches expected in the last quarter of the year.
Bulk explosives: pricing tied to raw material costs; more than 40 players in the segment; management declined to predict FY28.
RDX/HMX: international demand good, but licences difficult; management said war-driven demand has lifted prices for now.
Alternate raw material for mines/loitering munitions under DRDO, ARDE and HEMRL testing; management expects about 6 more months.
Naval opportunity linked to Apollo association; potential to be clearer by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall from INR20 crore to INR11 crore, and is INR11 crore sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier quarters had expected credit loss provisions and forex losses that did not recur; a sustainable run rate of about INR9-10 crore per quarter was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin improve from the 35% level, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as the product mix and dispatches improve; it reiterated the 15-20% EBITDA target and did not quantify a gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the roughly INR400 crore of export licences, and what export revenue is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Several licences received in the past week, with material moving; INR150-200 crore of export is targeted in Q2, and prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR430 crore October 2025 order on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 execution was about INR21 crore, the order will be fully executed in FY27 (not two-thirds), and capacity is available with chaff imports already executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Defence revenue fall 35%, and was it procurement or acceptance delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to export licence and component import delays, and said customer procurement and acceptance were not a cause; completion expected in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook if raw material prices normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material prices are not normalising yet; contracts already signed must be executed first, then prices will be raised. The 15-20% EBITDA target is for this financial year.

risks_watch: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to about 6% (per analyst calculation) from about 15% in the prior year, with raw material cost and under-absorption cited; recovery to 15-20% depends on contracts and price pass-through.
FY27 revenue of INR600 crore needs INR500-600 crore in 9 months after INR103 crore in Q1; Chaff imports remain dependent on conditions abroad.
Export licence timing (3-4 months processing plus importing-country licence) could delay the INR350 crore April 2026 order.
Katepally commissioning relies on water trials in September and imported mixer parts; any slippage pushes production later.
Andhra Pradesh expansion land pricing unresolved; Apollo's stance on expansion not yet confirmed.
Pending LD (liquidated damages) reversal of about INR30 crore on the July 2023 flares order, expected by October-November 2026.
Unclear Apollo synergy details; management said more to come next quarter.
